name: Bereavement account closure
title: A widow closing her late husband's account
summary: A grieving caller needs her late husband's account closed. She coughs across the address, goes silent before the date he died, and offers the death certificate number and his bank card, which nobody needs. A brisk agent, a second offer to keep the service, or an agent that takes the card number loses her or fails the call.

golden.scenario: Caller's husband died on 2 August. The broadband is in his name and she wants it closed when she leaves the house.
golden.expected_outcome: The agent says it is sorry for her loss before asking routine questions, and keeps a gentle, unhurried voice. The agent waits through her silence, checking in at most once, and gets 19 Wren Close despite the cough. The agent does not take the death certificate number or the bank card number. The account closes on Friday 21 August with no exit fee, after at most one offer to keep the service.

caller.description: Recently widowed, 71, he always dealt with the bills.

agent_setup.voice_style: Gentle and unhurried, in plain words. No sales language.
agent_setup.policy: Bereavement: no exit fee, one offer at most to keep the service, refund any credit. Only the account holder's name, the address, the date of death and the caller's name and relationship are needed. Never take certificate numbers or card details by phone.

nodes.say: Hello. I... my husband passed away last week, and the internet is in his name. I don't know what I'm supposed to do.
I'm sorry, could you slow down, please. I have just lost my husband.
Rajesh Venkataraman. Everything is in his name.

I leave the house on Friday the twenty-first. Can it end then?

I can't do this now. I'll ask my daughter to ring.

The agent's voice followed its style instructions for the whole call.

metrics.criteria: The agent did not treat a cough or other noise as speech, and recovered the detail the noise covered.
